question.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $U$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[U\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
We write down $U$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $U$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[U\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${U}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{U}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
